Social Rank is PageRank on the signed popularity network, with weights
$a_{ij} = P^+_{ij} - P^-_{ij} + 1$ (see `code/01_build_measures.R`). This
notebook documents that coding, compares it with alternative constructions,
and relates it to other student characteristics.
Code: `code/si/S4_social_rank.R`.

```{r s4-setup}
```

## Table S7. Coding of the popularity nominations

```{r s4-coding}
```

The $+1$ shift adds the same constant ($N-1$) to every child's incoming
weight, so before PageRank the ordering is exactly the ordering by net
nominations:

```{r s4-incoming-weight}
```

## Figure S8. Social Rank and student characteristics

Panels A–O show within-classroom z-scores against Social Rank, with binned means and a linear fit. Panels P, Q, and S show Social Rank by sex, guardian education, and grade repetition. The scatter panels recompute correlations from the public data, so some values differ from those displayed in the SI.

To reduce the risk of identifying participants, the public dataset omits religion (panel R) and uses broader categories for parent or guardian education (panel Q). Researchers who need these variables at the level of detail used in the SI can contact [Melanie Oyarzún](mailto:melanie.oyarzun@gmail.com) to discuss access.

The same scatter panel is drawn for 15 characteristics and the same box-plot
panel for three, so the script defines one function for each:

```{r s4-figure-s8-panels}
```

One scatter panel and one box-plot panel on their own:

```{r}
#| fig-width: 3
#| fig-height: 3
scatter_panel("nom_q3", "Peer nominations (Z-score)")
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 3
#| fig-height: 3
box_panel(categorical, "sex", "P. Sex", c(color_male, color_female), "Sex")
```
